_comment: M10 / R5.2: weather variants layered on top of whichever data/config/art.json time-of-day preset world_look.gd currently has applied -- a rainy noon and a clear noon share the same sun angle and only differ in what weather actually changes. world_weather.gd reads this file; world_look.gd's set_weather() merges each preset's sun/sky/environment keys the same way a `times` entry merges over the base block. All numbers here are TUNABLE.
_comment_cycle: How long one weather state holds before world_weather.gd rolls a new one, in real seconds. Wide range on purpose -- a fixed interval reads as a scripted flicker, not weather.

clear._comment: No sun/sky/environment override -- whatever the active time-of-day preset already set. Present so it is a real, selectable state (survey/debug included) rather than an implicit absence.

cloudy._comment: A stylised flat-overcast look, not literal cloud shapes -- world_look.gd's own header already states why: a ProceduralSkyMaterial can produce a gradient and a soft sun blob and nothing else. 'Cloudy' here means a dimmer, flatter sky and lower-contrast light; the sun's own cast shadow stays on (world_look.gd::_apply_sun's comment has the real reason -- driving it off blanked the whole terrain under this renderer/Terrain3D combination, a worse defect than the shadow it was meant to soften).

fog._comment: Ground-hugging haze, much denser than any time-of-day preset's own light depth-cueing fog. Sky pushed toward the fog colour (not the sun's own horizon colour) so distant terrain fades into a flat void instead of meeting a hard-edged horizon band -- the exact seam EV8 already fixed once for the ordinary time-of-day fog.

rain._comment: Cloudy plus falling rain plus a cooler, wetter ambient. Shares the cloudy sky family rather than inventing a third palette -- rain reads as 'cloudy, and now it is raining', not a fourth unrelated mood.
